statements.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). For either positive design-value profile
\[
 w_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P)
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 w_d=\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
\]
the least constant making every treatment-aware prediction-order implication
\[
 R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)\Longrightarrow w_d\le Cw_{d'}
 \qquad(d,d'\in\mathcal D)
\]
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)}}
 \frac{w_d}{w_{d'}}. \tag{1}
\]
For the arm-normalized profile, the smallest constant for the actual best-tie selector is \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)\); for the IKM-normalized profile it is \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P)\). Each is at most (1) for its profile and is finite at a fixed regular law. Consequently, a uniform constant over a nonempty law class exists exactly when the supremum of the corresponding best-tie ratio is finite.

If a numerical realization of \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) represents \(R_d^A(P)\) by a positive quadratic form \(Q_{R,d}^A\{x_d(P)\}\) and represents the arm-normalized value by the profiled source-score form \(F_d\{x_d(P)\}\), then the two-sided envelope
\[
 0<\Lambda_-^A(P):=\min_d\inf_x\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}^A(x)}
 \le
 \max_d\sup_x\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}^A(x)}=:\Lambda_+^A(P)<\infty
\]
implies
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)
 \le\max_{\substack{d,d':\,R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}
 \le\frac{\Lambda_+^A(P)}{\Lambda_-^A(P)}. \tag{2}
\]
As for the unadjusted rule, this envelope is generally conservative and the sharp constant is not generally a largest generalized eigenvalue, because profiling the two source terms produces a nonquadratic numerator and equality additionally requires saturation by law-realized, treatment-aware-risk-ordered directions.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix one of the two profiles in the statement and write its values as \(w_d\).  For the arm-normalized profile, strict positivity and finiteness follow from Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\), positive unit costs, and Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\).  For the IKM-normalized profile, Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}source\text{-}arm\text{-}positivity}\) gives \(0<1-p_{g,1}<1\); hence
\[
  0<V_{g,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
   =(1-p_{g,1})^2V_{g,d}<\infty,
\]
and Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}design\text{-}value}\) gives \(0<w_d<\infty\).  Thus, for either profile, all ratios below are well defined and finite.

Define
\[
  \mathcal O_P^A
  =\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)\},
  \qquad
  C_{mathrm{ord}}^A(P;w)
  =\max_{(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P^A}\frac{w_d}{w_{d'}}.       \tag{18}
\]
The set is nonempty and finite because \(\mathcal D\) is nonempty and finite and every diagonal pair belongs to it.  If \(C\ge C_{mathrm{ord}}^A(P;w)\), every treatment-aware order implication follows immediately from (18).  Conversely, if every implication holds with \(C\), division by \(w_{d'}>0\) for each pair in \(\mathcal O_P^A\), followed by maximization, gives \(C\ge C_{mathrm{ord}}^A(P;w)\).  This proves (1) and its minimality.  It is the treatment-aware instance of the finite-order argument proved in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}predictive\text{-}operator\text{-}certificate}\).

Let
\[
  \bar w=\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}w_{d'},
  \qquad
  w_{mathrm{pred}}^A
  =\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{mathrm{pred}}^A(P)}w_d.
\]
The least best-tie selector constant is \(w_{mathrm{pred}}^A/\bar w\).  By Definitions~\(\mathrm{def{:}predictive\text{-}benchmark}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}design\text{-}value}\), this ratio is \(\rho_{mathrm{pred}}^A(P)\) for the arm-normalized profile and \(\rho_{mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P)\) for the IKM-normalized profile.  Choose \(d_A\) attaining \(w_{mathrm{pred}}^A\) within \(\mathcal D_{mathrm{pred}}^A(P)\), and choose \(d_0\) attaining \(\bar w\).  Since \(R_{d_A}^A(P)\le R_{d_0}^A(P)\), the pair \((d_A,d_0)\) occurs in (18), and therefore
\[
  1\le\frac{w_{mathrm{pred}}^A}{\bar w}
  \le C_{mathrm{ord}}^A(P;w)<\infty.                       \tag{19}
\]
The uniform-law-class equivalence follows pointwise: a finite uniform constant bounds the corresponding pointwise least ratio and hence its supremum, while a finite supremum itself supplies a uniform constant.

For the quadratic certificate, let
\[
  r_d^A(x)=\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}^A(x)}.
\]
Positivity of \(Q_{R,d}^A\) on the stated cones permits division.  The definitions of \(\Lambda_-^A(P)\) and \(\Lambda_+^A(P)\) imply, at every transported direction \(x_d(P)\),
\[
  \Lambda_-^A(P)R_d^A(P)
  \le\mathcal V_d^*(P)
  \le\Lambda_+^A(P)R_d^A(P).                              \tag{20}
\]
For any pair with \(R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)\), (20) gives
\[
 \mathcal V_d^*(P)
 \le\Lambda_+^A(P)R_d^A(P)
 \le\Lambda_+^A(P)R_{d'}^A(P)
 \le\frac{\Lambda_+^A(P)}{\Lambda_-^A(P)}
       \mathcal V_{d'}^*(P).                               \tag{21}
\]
Maximizing (21) over the treatment-aware order relation, and applying (19) with \(w_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P)\), proves (2).

Finally, changing the denominator from \(Q_{R,d}\) to \(Q_{R,d}^A\) does not change the profiled numerator \(F_d\).  Identity (9) and the explicit parallelogram-law failure (17) in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}predictive\text{-}operator\text{-}certificate}\) therefore apply unchanged.  A largest generalized eigenvalue for a fixed allocation supplies only an upper full-space quadratic envelope.  The exact treatment-aware constant additionally requires a positive lower envelope and equality along law-realized directions whose treatment-aware risks have the required ordering.  Absent those saturation conditions, (2) can be strict, so neither the pairwise sharp constant nor the best-tie sharp constant is generally a largest generalized eigenvalue.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\chi>1\) and \(B>0\). Every center \(P_\epsilon\), \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), belongs to \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\cap\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\), both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\),
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad D^*(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\},               \tag{1}
\]
and the paired costs and named criteria satisfy
\[
 C_{d_{\mathrm p}}=5\chi,
 \qquad C_{d_{\mathrm e}}=5,
\]
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon;B).      \tag{2}
\]
The variance values and fixed-\(\chi\) expansion are
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +\frac{896}{75(10\chi-3)},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\frac{3872}{25},
\]
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).                                  \tag{3}
\]
For each fixed \((\chi,\epsilon)\), there is \(r_\epsilon>0\) such that every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon\) belongs to \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\cap\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\), has both bridge contrasts equal to \(\tau\), and satisfies
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)
 =\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\},                         \tag{4}
\]
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)>\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_\epsilon;B),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)>\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon). \tag{5}
\]
For every fixed law in this ball, there is a finite \(B_0(P)\) such that
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}
 \quad\text{for every }B\ge B_0(P).                       \tag{6}
\]
No equality between \(r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\) and \(R_d(P)\) is asserted away from the centers.
statements.proof_tex:
All center assertions follow from Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\). We prove the neighborhood assertion while keeping the CLW affine residual and the unrestricted risk distinct away from the centers.

The center lies in the relative interior of the finite-cell parameterization. Strict positivity of every cell, source and treatment overlap, and nonzero determinants of the finite completeness and bridge-operator matrices are open conditions. Matrix inversion is continuous away from zero determinant. The constrained factorization continues to impose consistency, experimental randomization, latent observational exchangeability, source-invariant proxy kernels, source support, and conditional proxy independence. It therefore preserves the causal and sequential restrictions on a sufficiently small relative ball. The bridge solutions, their source-score moments, and their positive profiles are rational functions of the positive cell probabilities and finite inverse matrices, hence are continuous there. Shrinking once more preserves finite strictly positive source-score variances.

The equality of both bridge contrasts with \(\tau\) is structural on the constrained family, not a continuity assertion. Indeed, \(Y(1)=Y(0)=U\), so \(\tau=0\). For either treatment arm, the outcome-bridge equation, the sequential restriction, and early-proxy completeness imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P\{h_d(S_{3d},a)\mid U,A=a,G=O\}
 =\mathbb E_P(Y\mid U,A=a,G=O)=U.
\]
Source invariance of the proxy kernels and experimental randomization then give
\[
 \mu_{d,a}
 =\mathbb E_P\{h_d(S_{3d},a)\mid A=a,G=E\}
 =\mathbb E_P(U),
\]
independently of \(a\). Hence \(\theta_d(P)=0=\tau\) for both designs throughout the ball.

For the named criterion, every entry of
\[
 \Gamma_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_d\xi_d^\top\mid G=O),
 \qquad g_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_dY\mid G=O)
\]
is continuous in the positive finite-cell vector. The full determinant is nonzero at the center and remains nonzero after shrinking. On that neighborhood,
\[
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)
 =\mathbb E_P(Y^2\mid G=O)
 -g_d(P)^\top\Gamma_d(P)^{-1}g_d(P)                       \tag{32}
\]
is continuous. This proves persistence of CLW admissibility and continuity of the actual CLW objective. Separately,
\[
 R_d(P)=\mathbb E_P\{\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X,Z_{M_d},G=O)\mid G=O\}
\]
is a finite sum of cell probabilities and ratios having positive denominators, and is continuous without being equated to (32).

The named CLW, unrestricted-risk, and bridge-value optimizer gaps are all strict at the center by the sharp-elbow lemma. Finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) permits a common positive radius preserving every ordering. The ratio denominators remain positive, and continuity permits a further shrinking that gives both one-half inequalities. For any fixed law in the resulting ball, the floor inequality from the sharp-elbow proof gives
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)
 \longrightarrow C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P).
\]
The strict continuous gap and finite catalogue furnish a finite law-specific \(B_0(P)\) beyond which the integer selector is \(\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\). This proves every assertion.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\chi>1\), \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), and \(B>0\), and write \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}=P_\epsilon\). For a binary center design with early and late signals \(x,y\in(0,1)\), the nonredundant affine regressor is \(\xi_d=(1,W_x,W_y)^\top\), its full Gram matrix and determinant are
\[
 \Gamma_d(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&xy\\0&xy&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \det\Gamma_d(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=1-x^2y^2>0,              \tag{1}
\]
and its population affine projection has intercept zero and coefficients
\[
 \beta_1=\frac{x(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2},
 \qquad
 \beta_2=\frac{y(1-x^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.                       \tag{2}
\]
Consequently the distinct CLW affine residual and the unrestricted unadjusted risk agree at the center, with
\[
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =R_d(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.                 \tag{3}
\]
Thus \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\cap\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\), both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\), and
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B). \tag{4}
\]
At the same centers,
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}
 {1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac35
 =R_{d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}).                  \tag{5}
\]
Hence
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad
 D^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}.              \tag{6}
\]
There is a finite \(B_0(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\) such that
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\{d_{\mathrm p}\}
 \quad\text{for every }B\ge B_0(P_{\chi,\epsilon}).      \tag{7}
\]
The selected design is costlier in each source:
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =\frac{5(\chi-1)}2>0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{40\chi}{10\chi-3},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}(\epsilon^{-2}+14),
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\frac{3872}{25}.
\]
All four named-CLW and unadjusted-risk center ratios agree:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 &=\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac{25}{3872}
 \left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{20\chi(5\chi-1)}{10\chi-3}}
 +\sqrt{\frac{32(5\chi+1)}{75(10\chi-3)}
 (\epsilon^{-2}+14)}
 \right\}^{2}.                                            \tag{8}
\end{aligned}
\]
Every ratio in (8) exceeds \((\epsilon^{-2}+14)/726\). For all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), its infimum over \(\chi>1\) is attained; every minimizer satisfies
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},             \tag{9}
\]
and the sharp optimized elbow is
\[
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}),                                      \tag{10}
\]
where \(\rho\) is any of the four center ratios in (8).
statements.proof_tex:
By Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}clw\text{-}population\text{-}design\text{-}rule}\), under its transported complete-randomization and arm-homoskedastic specialization the published population criterion is affine-linear residual variance divided by sample size. Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}clw\text{-}linear\text{-}cost\text{-}selector}\) maps the support only to \(M_d\) and imposes \(c(M_d,n)=nC_d\), so the continuous criterion is \(C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)/B\).

We first compute both residuals. Since \(X\) has one-point support, \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\) is zero-dimensional and \(\xi_d=(1,W_x,W_y)^\top\). Symmetry and conditional independence given \(U\) give
\[
 \mathbb E(U)=\mathbb E(W_x)=\mathbb E(W_y)=0,
 \quad \mathbb E(UW_x)=x,
 \quad \mathbb E(UW_y)=y,
 \quad \mathbb E(W_xW_y)=xy.                              \tag{11}
\]
Therefore the full affine Gram matrix, including its unique intercept, and the outcome cross moment are
\[
 \Gamma_d(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&xy\\0&xy&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad \det\Gamma_d(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=1-x^2y^2>0,
 \qquad g_d(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=(0,x,y)^\top.              \tag{12}
\]
The intercept coefficient is zero, and inversion of the lower \(2\)-by-\(2\) block gives
\[
 \beta_1=\frac{x(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2},
 \qquad
 \beta_2=\frac{y(1-x^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.                       \tag{13}
\]
The projection identity now yields
\[
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =1-(x,y)
 \begin{pmatrix}1&xy\\xy&1\end{pmatrix}^{-1}
 \begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}
 =\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.                        \tag{14}
\]
For the unrestricted risk, if \(r,s\in\{-1,1\}\), then
\[
 P(W_x=r,W_y=s\mid G=O)=\frac{1+xyrs}{4},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E(U\mid W_x=r,W_y=s,G=O)=\frac{xr+ys}{1+xyrs}.
\]
Since \(U^2=1\), the conditional-mean projection gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R_d(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=1-\frac{1}{2}\left\{
 \frac{(x+y)^2}{1+xy}+\frac{(x-y)^2}{1-xy}\right\}\\
 &=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}
 =r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}).                 \tag{15}
\end{aligned}
\]
This equality has been proved only at the symmetric centers. Also, \(Y(1)=Y(0)=U\) and \(Z(1)=Z(0)\), so the affine residual law is identical in the two arms of the transported randomized comparison. Thus the transported arm-homoskedastic condition holds; finite support gives all moment conditions; and (12) proves full-Gram admissibility.

We next verify regularity rather than assume it. All center latent cells are strictly positive. Consistency is built into the potential variables. In source \(E\), \(T\) is independent of \((U,Z(0),Z(1),Y(0),Y(1))\); in source \(O\), conditioning on \(U\) makes treatment independent of the potential variables, with treatment probabilities in \([3/8,5/8]\). The law of \((U,Z(0),Z(1),X)\) is source-invariant, and every required source-support ratio is finite. Conditional independence of the proxies given \(U\) proves the sequential-outcome restriction. For a design with early signal \(x\ne0\) and late signal \(y\ne0\), the two binary conditional-expectation matrices in the completeness restrictions have nonzero determinants proportional to \(x(1-1/16)\) and \(y(1-1/16)\), respectively. The designwise matrix mapping the late proxy to the early proxy conditional on an observational treatment arm has nonzero determinant proportional to \(xy(1-1/16)\). Hence both completeness conditions and bijectivity of \(T_d\) hold.

The displayed candidates in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\) solve the bridge equations. Indeed, conditional proxy independence gives
\[
 \mathbb E\{W_y/y\mid W_x,A,G=O\}
 =\mathbb E(U\mid W_x,A,G=O)=\mathbb E(Y\mid W_x,A,G=O).
\]
Writing \(t=2a-1\), direct Bayes calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E(W_x\mid W_y=l,T=t,G=O)
 =x\frac{t/4+yl}{1+tyl/4}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E\left[\frac{16}{15}\left(1-\frac{tW_x}{4x}\right)
 \mathrel{\Big|}W_y=l,T=t,G=O\right]
 =\frac{1}{1+tyl/4},                                      \tag{16}
\]
which is exactly the experimental-to-observational density ratio for \(W_y\) conditional on the treatment arm. Thus the selection bridge also exists. The explicit variances computed below are finite and strictly positive. We have therefore verified every membership condition in \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), as well as membership in \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\). Finally, experimental randomization and \(\mathbb E(U)=0\) imply \(\mu_{d,a}=0\) for both arms, while \(Y(1)-Y(0)=0\). Hence both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\).

Substitute \((x,y)=(\epsilon,y_\chi)\) for \(d_{\mathrm p}\) and \((x,y)=(1/2,1/2)\) for \(d_{\mathrm e}\). Equations (14)--(15) give
\[
 r_{d_{\mathrm p}}^{\mathrm{lin}}
 =R_{d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}
 \frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))},
 \qquad
 r_{d_{\mathrm e}}^{\mathrm{lin}}=R_{d_{\mathrm e}}=\frac{3}{5}. \tag{17}
\]
Since \(C_{d_{\mathrm p}}=5\chi\) and \(C_{d_{\mathrm e}}=5\),
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{3}{2}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac{3}{2}<3=B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}.       \tag{18}
\]
The inequality is strict because \(0<y_\chi<1\). Equation (17) also gives the raw-risk chain in the statement. Hence both continuous selectors choose \(d_{\mathrm p}\).

For the integer selector, if \(B\ge2C_d\), then
\[
 0\le \frac{B}{\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor}-C_d
 \le\frac{2C_d^2}{B}.                                     \tag{19}
\]
Multiplication by \(r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\) gives
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 \longrightarrow C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}). \tag{20}
\]
The catalogue is finite and the gap in (18) is strict, so a finite \(B_0(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\) preserves the singleton integer selector for every larger budget. The primitive cost formulas also give
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =\frac{5(\chi-1)}2>0.                                    \tag{21}
\]

It remains to compute the source-score profiles. With \(t=2a-1\), \(h_d(W_y,a)=W_y/y\), \(\mu_{d,a}=0\), and \(p_{g,a}=1/2\),
\[
 \phi_{E,d}=\frac{2TW_y}{y},
 \qquad V_{E,d}=\frac{4}{y^2}.                            \tag{22}
\]
For the observational score,
\[
 \phi_{O,d}=2T\frac{16}{15}left(1-\frac{TW_x}{4x}\right)
 \left(U-\frac{W_y}{y}\right).
\]
Conditional on \(U\), the pair \((T,W_x)\) is independent of \(W_y\), and
\[
 \mathbb E\left[\left(1-\frac{TW_x}{4x}\right)^2\mathrel{\Big|}U\right]
 =\frac{1+14x^2}{16x^2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\left[\left(U-\frac{W_y}{y}\right)^2\mathrel{\Big|}U\right]
 =\frac{1-y^2}{y^2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 V_{O,d}=\frac{64(1-y^2)(1+14x^2)}{225x^2y^2}.             \tag{23}
\]
At the two designs these identities become
\[
 V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{40\chi}{10\chi-3},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}(\epsilon^{-2}+14),              \tag{24}
\]
\[
 V_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=16,
 \qquad V_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=\frac{384}{25}.
\]
Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) now gives
\[
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*
 =\left(\sqrt{2\cdot16}+\sqrt{3\cdot384/25}\right)^2
 =\frac{3872}{25},                                        \tag{25}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm p}}^*}{\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*}
 =\frac{25}{3872}
 \left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{20\chi(5\chi-1)}{10\chi-3}}
 +\sqrt{\frac{32(5\chi+1)}{75(10\chi-3)}
 (\epsilon^{-2}+14)}
 \right\}^{2}.                                            \tag{26}
\]
Dropping the first nonnegative square-root term in (26) gives
\[
 \frac{\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm p}}^*}{\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*}
 \ge\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}(\epsilon^{-2}+14)
 >\frac{\epsilon^{-2}+14}{726}>1,                         \tag{27}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\). Thus \(D^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and the named and raw-risk ratios both equal (26).

At every center \(p_{E,1}=p_{O,1}=1/2\). Hence
\[
 V_{g,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac{1}{4}V_{g,d},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*=\frac{1}{4}\mathcal V_d^*,
 \qquad g\in\{E,O\}.                                    \tag{28}
\]
The common factor preserves the optimizer and cancels from every best-tie ratio. This proves the four ratio equalities and the IKM optimizer claim. For fixed \(\chi\), expansion of (26) gives
\[
 \rho(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).                                  \tag{29}
\]

Finally we optimize the exact center ratio. Define the proof intermediates
\[
 A(\chi)=10\chi+1+\frac{3}{10\chi-3},
 \qquad
 D(\chi)=\frac{16}{75}+\frac{16}{15(10\chi-3)},
 \qquad C_0=\frac{25}{3872}.
\]
Equation (26) is equivalently
\[
 \epsilon^2\rho
 =C_0\left[
 \epsilon^2A(\chi)+D(\chi)(1+14\epsilon^2)
 +2\epsilon\sqrt{1+14\epsilon^2}\sqrt{A(\chi)D(\chi)}
 \right].                                                 \tag{30}
\]
Set \(\chi=k\epsilon^{-2/3}\). Locally uniformly for \(k\) in compact subsets of \((0,\infty)\),
\[
 \epsilon^2\rho
 =\frac{1}{726}+C_0\epsilon^{2/3}
 \left\{2\sqrt{\frac{32k}{15}}+\frac{8}{75k}\right\}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).                                      \tag{31}
\]
The exact positive terms in (30) show that the rescaled objective is coercive when \(k\downarrow0\) or \(k\uparrow\infty\). Comparison with any fixed positive \(k\) also excludes the boundary \(\chi\downarrow1\) for all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\). Thus the infimum is attained, all rescaled minimizers lie in one compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), and the locally uniform expansion applies to them. The bracket in (31) has derivative
\[
 \sqrt{\frac{32}{15}}k^{-1/2}-\frac{8}{75}k^{-2},
\]
which vanishes uniquely at
\[
 k_\star=\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}.
\]
At this point
\[
 C_0\left\{2\sqrt{\frac{32k_\star}{15}}+\frac{8}{75k_\star}\right\}
 =\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}.
\]
This proves (9)--(10), including the assertion for every minimizing factor.

statements.statement:
Fix any prescribed \(\chi>1\). Under the IKM score and profile normalization, every binary center law satisfies, for \(d\in\mathcal D\),
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{O,d},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon).
\]
Consequently \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)\). For each fixed \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), there is \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}>0\) such that every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) is regular, both admissible bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
On this neighborhood, the IKM-normalized profile is the profiled local causal semiparametric efficiency bound under the fixed-system conditions in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\).
statements.justification: Balanced treatment multiplies both source moments by one quarter, so profiling multiplies every center design value by one quarter and leaves the exact approximation ratio unchanged.
statements.gap: This transfers the arm-normalized impossibility to the published IKM score normalization without conflating the two normalizations.
statements.consumer: The lemma provides the normalized stability radius and the conditional fixed-system causal-efficiency interpretation used by the main impossibility theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
At every center the treatment probability in each source is one half. Hence, for \(g\in\{E,O\}\),
\[
 \psi_{g,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac{1}{2}\phi_{g,d},
 \qquad
 V_{g,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac{1}{4}V_{g,d}.               \tag{33}
\]
Taking square roots in the profile and then squaring gives
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{1}{4}\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon).                  \tag{34}
\]
The common factor leaves the strict optimizer and best-tie ratio unchanged. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) and Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\) therefore prove all center assertions.

The latter lemma supplies a constrained-model ball on which regularity, common identification, and raw-risk choice persist. On that ball, source treatment probabilities, finite bridge inverses, source-score moments, and IKM profiles are continuous functions of the positive finite-cell coordinates. The IKM optimizer gap is strict at the center and its ratio denominator is positive. Shrinking the ball preserves the optimizer and makes the ratio exceed one half of its center value. Under the additional fixed-system premises of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\), that cited result identifies the IKM profile as the profiled local causal efficiency bound. No efficiency interpretation is inferred from (33)--(34) without those premises.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), the exact fixed-catalogue raw-risk-selection identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(R_d(P)\le R_{d'}(P)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,R_d(P)\le R_{d'}(P)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\). Nevertheless, for every prescribed finite \(\chi>1\), the \(\chi\)-indexed binary region satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\), even though the uniquely raw-risk-selected design has paired cost \(\chi\) times that of the arm-normalized source-score-optimal design at the center laws. Across all center cost-disadvantage factors, every minimizing sequence satisfies
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},
\]
and the exact least-divergent envelope obeys
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform raw-risk-to-source-score guarantee; optimizing the witness's cost disadvantage does not remove the leading \(1/(726\epsilon^2)\) divergence.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Positive costs, Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\), and Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) give
\[
 0<\mathcal V_d^*(P)
 =\left(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}\right)^2
 <\infty                                                    \tag{35}
\]
for every design. Since \(\mathcal D\) is finite and nonempty, both the global minimizer set and \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) are nonempty. Substitution of (35) into the definition of \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) proves the identity. Its numerator minimizes over a subset of the denominator's index set, so the ratio is at least one; (35) makes it finite.

The actual best-tie selected-value inequality holds with constant \(C\) exactly when \(C\) is at least the displayed ratio, proving minimality. For the pairwise implications, every valid \(C(P)\) must dominate \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\) for each ordered pair satisfying \(R_d(P)\le R_{d'}(P)\). Conversely, the maximum of these finitely many positive ratios dominates every such pair and therefore makes every implication true. This proves the exact pairwise constant and its finiteness.

Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}predictive\text{-}impossibility}\) and Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) supply the secondary generic raw-risk conclusions. Each binary region contains every one of its centers, and the center ratio exceeds \((\epsilon^{-2}+14)/726\); hence the supremum is infinite as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\). At a center, the selected design has paired cost \(5\chi\), the optimal design has paired cost \(5\), and their ratio is \(\chi\). The same sharp-elbow lemma proves the minimizing scale and the displayed expansion for both generic center ratios. Thus exact fixed-law enumeration does not imply a law-uniform guarantee.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\chi>1\) and \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\). For a binary center design having early and late proxy signals \(x,y\in(0,1)\), its treatment-aware observational prediction risk is
\[
 \mathcal R_A(x,y)=
 \frac{15(1-x^2)(1-y^2)(16-x^2-y^2-14x^2y^2)}
 {\{16(1+xy)^2-(x+y)^2\}\{16(1-xy)^2-(x-y)^2\}}. \tag{1}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm e}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\frac{585}{1024},
 \qquad
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 \le R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac{585}{1024}. \tag{2}
\]
Thus
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
\]
and, at every center,
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}). \tag{3}
\]
Hence the exact ratio, the lower bound \((\epsilon^{-2}+14)/726\), the optimizing scale \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\sim(\sqrt[3]{18}/15)\epsilon^{-2/3}\), and the sharp second-order expansion in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) hold unchanged for both treatment-aware ratios.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix center signals \(x,y\in(0,1)\) and write \(T=2A-1\). Under the observational center law, the joint mass of \((T,W_x,W_y,U)=(t,r,s,u)\), apart from its common positive normalizing factor, is
\[
 (1+tu/4)(1+xur)(1+yus).                                  \tag{36}
\]
Summing (36) over \(u\), first without and then with multiplication by \(u\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E(U\mid T=t,W_x=r,W_y=s)
 =\frac{t/4+xr+ys+txy\,rs/4}
 {1+txr/4+tys/4+xy\,rs}.                                  \tag{37}
\]
Every denominator in (37) is positive because all underlying cells are strictly positive. Since \(U^2=1\), the optimal squared-error risk is the expectation of one minus the square of (37). Substitution of the eight cell probabilities, grouping the terms paired by \((t,r,s)\mapsto(-t,-r,-s)\), and collecting even powers yields
\[
 \mathcal R_A(x,y)=
 \frac{15(1-x^2)(1-y^2)(16-x^2-y^2-14x^2y^2)}
 {\{16(1+xy)^2-(x+y)^2\}\{16(1-xy)^2-(x-y)^2\}}.         \tag{38}
\]
This is a finite algebraic evaluation of the conditional-variance functional defining \(R_d^A(P)\).

Substitution of \(x=y=1/2\) gives
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm e}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\frac{585}{1024}.
\]
Adding \(A\) to a squared-error predictor cannot increase its projection risk. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) therefore gives
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 \le R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac{3}{10}<\frac{585}{1024}.         \tag{39}
\]
Thus both generic selector sets are the singleton \(\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\). Under either profile their ratio numerators are consequently identical, proving both equalities in (3). The exact ratio, lower bound, minimizing scale, and sharp expansion then transfer directly from the sharp-elbow lemma.

statements.statement:
For each fixed \(\chi>1\) and \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the radii \(r_\epsilon\) and \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) in Lemmas~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\) may be jointly decreased, without losing any conclusion of those lemmas, so that every law in the corresponding smaller finite-cell ball also satisfies
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)>\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P_\epsilon),
\]
and, in the IKM-normalized ball,
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
Thus the radii used to form \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) can preserve both strict prediction-risk orderings simultaneously with the arm-normalized and IKM-normalized optimizer orderings.
statements.proof_tex:
At the center, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}treatment\text{-}aware\text{-}sharp\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) gives a strict treatment-aware risk gap. On the positive finite-cell model,
\[
 R_d^A(P)=\mathbb E_P\{\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid A,X,Z_{M_d},G=O)\mid G=O\}, \tag{40}
\]
which is a finite sum of cell masses and conditional-moment ratios with strictly positive denominators. Hence (40) is continuous in the relative finite-cell topology.

Intersect each ball already furnished by Lemmas~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\) with a sufficiently small relative open neighborhood on which the strict treatment-aware ordering persists. The treatment-aware best-tie set is then \(\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\). The arm-normalized and IKM-normalized profiles and their positive minima are continuous on these smaller balls, so both treatment-aware ratios are continuous there. One further shrinking makes each ratio exceed one half of its center value. Decreasing a radius cannot destroy any conclusion valid on the larger ball, including regularity, common identification, full-Gram CLW admissibility, the named continuous ordering, raw-risk ordering, bridge-profile orderings, or the law-specific eventual integer-selector conclusion. This proves simultaneous stability.

statements.statement:
Fix \(B>0\), and choose the radii defining \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) after the joint shrinking in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}joint\text{-}predictive\text{-}binary\text{-}stability}\). Then every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular, CLW-admissible, and common-identifying, and
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)
 =\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)
 =\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}.                         \tag{1}
\]
For every fixed \(P\) in this region, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\) for all \(B\ge B_0(P)\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)
 =\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)
 =\infty.                                                   \tag{2}
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) additionally satisfies \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P;B)
 =\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\infty.                                                   \tag{3}
\]
At every center all six ratios in (2)--(3) agree. For fixed \(\chi>1\), their common value satisfies
\[
 \rho(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}),
 \qquad
 \frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}
 =\frac1{726}+\frac5{726(10\chi-3)}>\frac1{726}.          \tag{4}
\]
After optimizing the exact common center ratio over \(\chi>1\), every minimizer satisfies
\[
 \chi\sim\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},         \tag{5}
\]
and each of the six optimized center envelopes obeys
\[
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).                                       \tag{6}
\]
The named conclusion is only for the CLW population affine-linear rule under its stated transport. The unrestricted-risk conclusions are secondary and no assertion concerns CLW's empirical equation~(3.6), OGA, original RCT theorem, arbitrary predictive procedures, persistent-confounding analysis, or bridge-role choice.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\chi>1\). Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\) permits the radii in \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) to be chosen so that every member is regular, CLW-admissible, and common-identifying, with the named CLW selector, raw-risk selector, and arm-normalized optimizer asserted in (1). Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}joint\text{-}predictive\text{-}binary\text{-}stability}\) decreases the same radii while preserving those conclusions and adding the treatment-aware selector identity. The floor conclusion follows pointwise from the law-specific threshold in the binary-stability lemma.

Every center belongs to its defining ball. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) proves equality of the named ratios and the unadjusted generic ratios, while Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}treatment\text{-}aware\text{-}sharp\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) adds equality of both treatment-aware ratios. Their common value exceeds \((\epsilon^{-2}+14)/726\). Letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) proves all three arm-normalized suprema in (2). On \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\), the IKM-stability and joint-stability lemmas preserve the strict IKM optimizer and more than one half of each diverging center ratio, proving (3).

For fixed \(\chi\), expansion of the exact common center ratio in the sharp-elbow lemma gives (4). Its coefficient satisfies the exact identity
\[
 \frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}-\frac{1}{726}
 =\frac{5}{726(10\chi-3)}>0.                              \tag{41}
\]
The rescaled optimization in that lemma proves (5)--(6), and equality of all six center ratios transfers the conclusions to each envelope. The final scope qualifications follow from the construction: only the transported CLW population affine-linear criterion maps support to \(M_d\); the two unrestricted risks are separate secondary functionals, and none of the other listed procedures appears in an assumption or algebraic step.

First fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\) and \(B>0\). The finite-moment and full-Gram conditions make each \(r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\), and hence each named criterion, finite. Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) and Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\) give \(0<\mathcal V_d^*(P)<\infty\). Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}source\text{-}arm\text{-}positivity}\) implies \(0<(1-p_{g,1})^2<1\), so every IKM profile is also finite and strictly positive. The finite named selector is nonempty. Direct substitution of the budget-profile formula into the definition of \(\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}\) proves (1), and (2) is its IKM analogue. In each case the numerator minimizes over a nonempty subset of the denominator's index set, giving a finite ratio at least one. The selected-value inequality holds precisely for constants no smaller than that ratio, proving best-tie minimality.

For either positive profile \(w_d\), define the proof intermediate
\[
 C_{\mathrm{ord}}^{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)
 =\max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)
 \le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}\frac{w_d}{w_{d'}}.       \tag{42}
\]
The index set is finite and contains every diagonal pair. Any constant satisfying all named-rule order implications must dominate every indexed ratio, whereas (42) itself satisfies every implication. This proves (3). On the domain where all compared integer counts are positive, replacing the continuous criterion by \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}\) proves the integer claim verbatim. Computing the \(|\mathcal D|\) criteria and minima is linear in \(|\mathcal D|\); enumerating all ordered pairs uses at most \(|\mathcal D|^2\) comparisons.

Now, independently, fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). The generic unadjusted identity and its positivity are Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}finite\text{-}catalogue\text{-}predictive\text{-}guarantee}\). The same direct substitution proves the treatment-aware identity in (4) and both IKM identities. Repeating (42) with \(R_d(P)\) or \(R_d^A(P)\) as the ordering criterion proves the exact generic pairwise maxima. This argument uses only observable-class positivity and does not place the generic law in the narrower CLW domain.

Finally, Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}two\text{-}rule\text{-}predictive\text{-}impossibility}\) proves unbounded ratios for the named rule and both generic rules on the jointly shrunk regions. Lemmas~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}treatment\text{-}aware\text{-}sharp\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) prove equality of all six center ratios and the common expansion (5). Thus the enumerations are exact and computable at each fixed law but yield no law-uniform constant.

Fix \(\chi>1\). Along the triangular center sequence, every observational cell of \((A,X,Z_{M_d})\) has probability bounded below by a positive constant depending only on \(\chi\), uniformly in \(m\). Indeed, the observational treatment kernels lie in \([3/8,5/8]\), the early signal belongs to \((0,10^{-3})\), the late signal \(y_\chi\) is fixed strictly below one, and the remaining signals equal \(1/2\). Also \(P(G=O)=1/2\). Standard binomial concentration applied to the finitely many cells therefore shows that every training and validation cell count is of order \(m\) with probability tending to one, and the probability of any zero denominator is exponentially small.

For a cell \(v=(a,x,z_{M_d})\), write
\[
 f_{d,m}^*(v)=\mathbb E_{P_{\chi,\epsilon_m}}(Y\mid A,X,Z_{M_d}=v,G=O).
\]
Both \(Y\) and every saturated cell mean lie in \([-1,1]\). Conditional on the cell counts, each nonempty-cell mean is an average of bounded independent variables, and its count is of order \(m\). A finite union bound over both designs and their finitely many cells gives
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max_v
 |\widehat f_{d,m}^A(v)-f_{d,m}^*(v)|=O_P(m^{-1/2}).        \tag{43}
\]
Conditional on the training half, the validation losses are independent and bounded by four. The same finite-class concentration argument gives
\[
 \max_d\left|\widehat R_{d,m}^A-
 \mathbb E\left[
 \{Y-\widehat f_{d,m}^A(A,X,Z_{M_d})\}^2
 \mathrel{\Big|}G=O,\mathcal I_{m,O}^{\mathrm{tr}}
 \right]\right|=O_P(m^{-1/2}).                            \tag{44}
\]
Because \(f_{d,m}^*\) is the conditional-mean projection, the cross term vanishes cell by cell and hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\mathbb E\left[
 \{Y-\widehat f_{d,m}^A(A,X,Z_{M_d})\}^2
 \mathrel{\Big|}G=O,\mathcal I_{m,O}^{\mathrm{tr}}
 \right]-R_d^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})\\
 &\qquad=
 \mathbb E\left[
 \{\widehat f_{d,m}^A(A,X,Z_{M_d})-f_{d,m}^*(A,X,Z_{M_d})\}^2
 \mathrel{\Big|}G=O,\mathcal I_{m,O}^{\mathrm{tr}}
 \right]
 =O_P(m^{-1}).                                             \tag{45}
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the last equality follows from (43) and the finite number of cells. Combining (44)--(45) proves (1).

Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}treatment\text{-}aware\text{-}sharp\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) gives, uniformly along the triangular sequence,
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})<\frac{3}{10},
 \qquad
 R_{d_{\mathrm e}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})=\frac{585}{1024}.
\]
The population gap is bounded below by \(585/1024-3/10>0\). The uniform empirical error in (1), together with deterministic tie breaking, therefore implies
\[
 P_{\chi,\epsilon_m}\{\widehat d_m^A=d_{\mathrm p}\}\longrightarrow1,
\]
which is (2).

On this event, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) identifies \(d_{\mathrm e}\) as the unique minimizer of both profiles and gives
\[
 \frac{\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm p}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})}
 {\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})}
 =\frac{\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm p},\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})}
 {\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e},\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})}
 >\frac{\epsilon_m^{-2}+14}{726}\longrightarrow\infty.  \tag{46}
\]
Since the event has probability tending to one, both random achieved ratios diverge in probability, proving (3). Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}independent\text{-}pilot}\) makes this pilot-only rule feasible before the main-study measurements are chosen. Its construction uses bounded finite-cell averages and no bridge inverse, inverse-problem learner, or growing sieve.

sampling_model.design: A full-catalogue pilot selects \(\widehat d_m\), computes the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\) from pilot estimates of both source-gradient variances and known costs, and fixes the integer counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\); an independent main study then measures the selected short-term outcomes in both samples and \(Y\) only in observational follow-up.
sampling_model.units: Independent superpopulation units from the experimental and observational populations, with implemented counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary complete randomization in the experimental sample and latent-confounded treatment in the observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment overlap within both sources and support overlap across sources are imposed designwise.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The pilot cross-fits both bridges and both score variances for every candidate. The main study refits the selected bridges with fixed-fold cross-fitting. Under the joint main-study law and uniformly over the finite design family and folds, the outcome-bridge weak and strong errors are \(O_P(\delta_{h,B})\) and \(O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), the selection-bridge weak and strong errors are \(O_P(\delta_{q,B})\) and \(O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), all four rates vanish, and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Pilot and main-study source-score second moments are uniformly \(O_P(r_{V,m})\) and \(O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) consistent under their respective laws, with both rates vanishing. The Wald variance uses the realized counts and selected foldwise second moments through \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\).

estimand_functional: The main statistical functional is the selected observed bridge contrast \(\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\) on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Its explicit selected-design cross-fitted estimator, studentizer, limit law, and Wald interval are given by Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}selected\text{-}wald\text{-}variance}\) and Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}postselection\text{-}wald}\), conditional on the declared selected-path learner, multiplier, pilot, and variance conditions. Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}postselection\text{-}wald\text{-}ate\text{-}corollary}\) converts this to inference for \(\tau\) on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\). Absolute fixed-system causal efficiency uses the IKM-normalized moments and the separately cited canonical-gradient conditions.
target_estimand: The causal estimand is \(\tau=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid G=O]\). The observable statistical target selected by the main theorem is \(\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)=\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\) on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\); it equals \(\tau\) only on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), which contains the binary witness region but not all of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).

tldr: Long-term experiments must choose which short-term outcomes to measure, which sequential proxy role each will play, and how to divide a fixed budget between randomized short-term units and observational long-term follow-up. In the persistent-confounding model of Imbens, Kallus, Mao, and Wang, the proposal makes that design the argument of the local semiparametric efficiency bound. A concrete binary two-design family proves that the uniquely optimal design under the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective, residual prediction variance divided by jointly budget-feasible sample size, can have an unbounded efficiency-loss ratio on a relatively open region even though every candidate remains identified and regular. The equal-cost witness makes the cost-aware ordering reduce exactly to its displayed residual-variance ordering; weakening only the selected design's early proxy then drives the selection bridge and observational gradient variance to infinity. The two source-specific variances also yield a pilot-feasible square-root allocation, integer sample counts, selection control by the oracle separation \(\gamma(P)\), and valid independent-main-sample Wald inference with an explicit selected-score variance estimator under the anchor's weak--strong bridge remainder condition uniformly over the finite design family.

project_justification.gap: The long-term data-combination literature treats the proxy system and sample share as fixed; surrogate-efficiency papers compare availability of a given surrogate vector, while Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm's cost-aware prediction design and other optimal-collection results do not cover persistent-confounding bridge geometry.
project_justification.niche: A finite costed catalogue with sequential role assignments creates nonnested inverse problems whose information contributions differ by source, so residual prediction variance divided by a jointly budget-feasible sample size need not order designs by their bridge-model efficiency values.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs an explicit regular equal-cost binary witness proving that the cost-aware prediction selector has no finite efficiency guarantee, derives the asymptotic budget-normalized design-value profile with an explicit floor-count residual, and implements both proxy-role choice and sample allocation from pilot gradient-variance estimates with oracle-separation selection control and selected-score Wald guarantees under designwise weak--strong bridge rates.

related_work: ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 supplies the persistent-confounding model and observed bridge equations: its Assumption 8 measures each bridge estimator in a weak conditional-moment metric and a strong \(L_2\) metric, its Theorem 4 proves estimator consistency, Theorem 5 gives the fixed-system asymptotic variance under the limiting sample-ratio convention when the better weak--strong cross-product is \(o(n^{-1/2})\), and Theorem 7 establishes the corresponding local semiparametric efficiency lower bound under bridge uniqueness and bijective \(T_d\). The design-value construction is informed by those fixed-system results and uses their weak--strong remainder geometry designwise over a finite family; it does not relabel Theorem 4 as an efficiency theorem. KallusMao2025 characterizes efficiency gains from a fixed surrogate vector when long-term outcomes are limited, but does not choose a costly set or sequential role. CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020, Section 3.2, equations (3.4)--(3.7), shows that in its completely randomized costly-covariate setting the MSE and power design objective is rewritten as residual prediction variance divided by sample size under budget. The comparator here applies that published-workflow-shaped objective to every admissible measurement design by charging \(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d}\) per paired experimental and follow-up observation; the equal-cost binary subclass then makes this cost-aware objective exactly proportional to residual prediction variance. The predictive-impossibility theorem gives a strict non-representability result: this cost-aware criterion has an unbounded prediction-to-efficiency ratio on a relatively open regular region. YangEcklesDhillonAral2024 warns that outcome prediction can differ from causal policy value but does not prove an efficiency-ratio impossibility. LalImbensHull2026 studies regularized combination versus naive screening in a linear latent-surrogate model, not inverse bridge design. TaoZengLin2020 and WangWangMiao2023 optimize phase-two sampling for a fixed measured-variable system. GuptaLiptonChilders2024 learns source allocations in generic moment models but leaves conditional-moment restrictions outside its theory. BennettKallusMaoNeweySyrgkanisUehara2023 supplies stable functional inference for weakly identified conditional moments, while ZhangLiMiaoTchetgenTchetgen2023 treats regular inference with nonunique bridges. MareisDrton2026 derives cost-aware staged measurement for a multivariate linear front-door model, not subset-role selection in the nonparametric long-term fusion model.
technical_internal_limitation: The binary witness establishes pointwise regularity for every positive weak-proxy signal, but its selection-bridge envelope is not uniform as the signal approaches zero; that nonuniform inverse geometry is precisely what generates the unbounded efficiency ratio. Equal costs isolate the inverse-geometry failure from the cost adjustment. The open positive problem is to characterize primitive operator comparability conditions that exclude this path without assuming a design-value bound directly.
honest_scope: The explicit binary family settles the absence of a universal approximation guarantee for residual prediction variance per jointly budget-feasible sample size while preserving identification and regularity design by design. Conditional on the stated finite-family-uniform weak and strong bridge rates, the weak--strong product remainder, and the two variance-estimation rates, the pilot-feasible allocation and post-selection Wald claims are theorem targets. The continuous budget profile is the \(B\to\infty\) limit of the floor-count bound, with the displayed nonnegative \(O(B^{-1})\) rounding residual. Population ties are retained in \(D^*(P)\); \(\gamma(P)\) controls only separation from nonoptimal designs and equals \(+\infty\) when every design is optimal. The sign of \(\Delta_P(d,d')\) is explanatory notation for comparing two profiled values and is not a solve target. A sharp finite guarantee under primitive operator comparability remains open. With a singleton design and fixed sample counts, the formulas reduce to Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem 5's variance and Theorem 7's local efficiency lower bound under their sample-ratio convention.
